passages.question: How do 401(k) deferrals and Section 125 premiums change income tax, Social Security and Medicare wages?
passages.excerpt: Elective employee contributions and deferrals to a plan containing a qualified cash or deferred compensation arrangement (401(k)). Generally exempt, but see section 402(g) for limitation. Taxable. Taxable. ... Cafeteria plan benefits under section 125. If employee chooses cash or other taxable benefit, subject to all employment taxes. If employee chooses a nontaxable benefit, the treatment is the same as if the benefit was provided outside the plan.

passages.question: When must Additional Medicare Tax be withheld from a paycheck?
passages.excerpt: In addition to withholding Medicare tax at 1.45%, you must withhold a 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax from wages you pay to an employee in excess of $200,000 in a calendar year. You’re required to begin withholding Additional Medicare Tax in the pay period in which you pay wages in excess of $200,000 to an employee and continue to withhold it each pay period until the end of the calendar year.

passages.question: When was each Q3 deposit due?
passages.excerpt: If you accumulate $100,000 or more in taxes on any day during a monthly or semiweekly deposit period ..., you must deposit the tax by the next business day, whether you’re a monthly or semiweekly schedule depositor. ... A business day is any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or legal holiday. ... The term “legal holiday” means any legal holiday in the District of Columbia. ... July 3—Independence Day (observed) September 7—Labor Day
